Have you had a severe or unusual headache at the same time?
Have you had pain in or around the affected eye?
Is the larger pupil on the same side as the drooping or abnormal eyelid?
Does the affected eye point downward and outward when you try to look straight ahead?
Do you have double vision?
Did these symptoms follow a head, neck, or eye injury?
Have you had weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, confusion, loss of balance, or loss of consciousness?
Have you had neck pain, facial pain, or a new drooping eyelid with a smaller pupil on that side?
Do the eyelid drooping or eye-movement problems fluctuate or worsen when you are tired?
Do they improve after rest?
Do you have weakness when chewing, swallowing, speaking, or holding your head up?
Do you have weakness in your arms or legs?
Have you had fever or a recent infection?
Is the eye red, swollen, or painful when you move it?
Have you noticed bulging of either eye?
Have you had weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, or a racing heartbeat?
Have you previously had similar episodes?
Do you have diabetes, high blood pressure, cancer, or a weakened immune system?
Have you recently used medications, eye drops, recreational drugs, or been exposed to chemicals that could affect pupil size?
Have you had a recent procedure or surgery involving your head, neck, chest, or eyes?
Have you ever been diagnosed with an aneurysm or other blood-vessel abnormality?

results: 1. Comprehensive neuro-ophthalmic examination, including visual acuity, visual fields, fundus examination, pupil measurements in bright and dim illumination, ocular motility in all directions, and assessment of ptosis
fundoscopy: normal
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides): not recorded
ocular motility examination: exotropia, hypotropia and motility impairment - a right oculomotor nerve palsy

pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
2. Review of old photographs and prior medical records for longstanding anisocoria, ptosis, or ocular misalignment
surgical history: not recorded
clinical course: not recorded
ocular surgical history: previous strabismus surgery and levator muscle surgery
3. MRI of the brain, cavernous sinuses, orbits, and brainstem with and without gadolinium contrast
MRI orbits: atrophy of the extraocular muscles, particularly the medial rectus - a long-standing, not acute, palsy
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
4. Magnetic resonance angiography of the circle of Willis and intracranial internal carotid arteries
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): NO aneurysm
5. Apraclonidine eye-drop testing
not performed / not available
6. Dilute pilocarpine eye-drop testing
not performed / not available
7. Serum acetylcholine-receptor and MuSK antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
8. Single-fiber electromyography of an appropriate facial muscle
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Long-standing congenital right oculomotor nerve palsy with aberrant regeneration causing a cyclic/spastic tonic pupil, with prior corrective strabismus and levator surgery

ALTERNATIVE: Adie tonic pupil

ALTERNATIVE: Pharmacological or postsurgical iris sphincter dysfunction causing an irregular tonic pupil
